name: Marble 60
notes: Marble veining as a coverage family: level N = N% vein material. Veins are the zero contours of band-passed Gaussian fields - smooth curves that never repeat - in a four-octave hierarchy, each octave's ridge modulated by a slow field so veins wax and wane along their length (without this the ridge is a plateau and sparse cuts shatter into chips - tried and rejected), everything sampled through one strong low-frequency domain warp: the marble flow. Nine NESTED thresholds of one veinness field (tips/marble.spec.json): thin primaries at 10 through breccia-like vein matrix at 90. Dual-gate train (mask 150% of the primary so vein features cross the stroke edge); levels 10-30 print through a sparser mask train so thin veins are not double-exposed. Verified comb-free and spike-free by tools/spectrum-audit.mjs; the vein anisotropy is local, so sector power stays within a few dB globally. Veins thicken toward bands; windows of clear stone shrink.
